name: button_esd
summary: A push button to ground behind a TVS and a series resistor, for a button on the board's edge under a finger
note: From simple_earring rev 2 (vendored with the bolt earring: boards/bolt-earring/vendor/simple_earring/scripts/circuit.py, whose comments give the reasons and the corner simulations behind each value). The TVS clamps a discharge at the switch's pad; R_SER then limits what reaches the node behind it (at a ~14 V clamp, ~14 mA through 1 kohm), which should have a capacitor of its own (power_latch's C_DEB) so a strike does not register as a press. R_SER costs a few tens of mV on the pressed level.

R_SER.note: Isolates the node behind from the clamp

OUT.note: Pulled to ground while pressed: the node must be pulled up

citations.quote: No terminal numbers are indicated on the Switches.
citations.note: Side-actuated B3U-3000P(M): the Terminal Arrangement/Internal Connections (Top View) figure shows terminals 2 and 1 joined by one contact. SW1's two pins are interchangeable; KiCad's SW_SPST_B3U-3000P footprint has pads 1 and 2.
Minimum applicable load (reference value). A press carries the pull-ups' current (in the bolt, power_latch's R_GATE and R_PRESS, about 70 uA), above it; the rating proper is 1 to 50 mA, 3 to 12 VDC.
Pin 2 is K2, cathode (diode 2): two back-to-back diodes, symmetric, so the pin order does not matter. KiCad's D_TVS (bidirectional) is A1 1, A2 2; D_SOD-882 has pads 1 and 2.

citations.quote: Bidirectional ESD protection of one line

citations.note: The button node sits at up to a full cell (4.2 V), under the standoff voltage.

citations.quote: IRM reverse leakage current VRWM = 5 V; Tamb = 25 °C - 5 100 nA
citations.note: Typ and max: a board-off leak into the button node (power_latch's LATCH_G budget); Fig. 6 gives its rise with temperature.
VCL max, the ~14 V clamp the note uses for R_SER's current.
